claims.text: H&P (pre-op) — Pre-op H&P timing: except in emergencies, before surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia the H&P must be completed and documented no more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission.
claims.quote: (1) Prior to surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia services and except in the case of emergencies: (i) A medical history and physical examination must be completed and documented no more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission or registration

claims.text: H&P (pre-op) — Pre-op update: when the H&P was done within the 30 days before admission, an updated exam noting any changes in condition must be completed and documented within 24 hours after admission.
claims.quote: (ii) An updated examination of the patient, including any changes in the patient's condition, must be completed and documented within 24 hours after admission or registration when the medical history and physical examination are completed within 30 days before admission or registration

claims.text: H&P (pre-op) — Consent: a properly executed informed consent form for the operation must be in the chart before surgery, except in emergencies.
claims.quote: (2) A properly executed informed consent form for the operation must be in the patient's chart before surgery, except in emergencies.

claims.text: Operative note — Operative report: describes techniques, findings, and tissues removed or altered; written or dictated immediately after surgery and signed by the surgeon.
claims.quote: (6) An operative report describing techniques, findings, and tissues removed or altered must be written or dictated immediately following surgery and signed by the surgeon.

claims.text: Progress (post-op) — Complications: document complications, hospital-acquired infections, and unfavorable reactions to drugs and anesthesia.
claims.quote: (iv) Documentation of complications, hospital acquired infections, and unfavorable reactions to drugs and anesthesia.

claims.text: Progress (post-op) — Progress: document the patient's progress, response to and changes in treatment, and any revision of the diagnosis.
claims.quote: You should document the patient's progress, response to and changes in treatment, and revision of diagnosis

claims.text: Consult — Consult results: the hospital record must contain the results of all consultative evaluations of the patient.
claims.quote: (iii) Results of all consultative evaluations of the patient and appropriate findings by clinical and other staff involved in the care of the patient.

claims.text: Consult — Billing a consult (Medicare): Medicare doesn't pay the CPT consultation codes (inpatient 99252-99255, office/outpatient 99242-99245); report the correct E/M visit code for the consult instead.
claims.quote: Medicare doesn't recognize these CPT codes for Part B payment purposes: Inpatient consultation codes, CPT codes 99252-99255 O/O consultation codes, CPT codes 99242-99245 Medicare recognizes these telehealth consultation codes for payment: HCPCS codes G0406-G0408 HCPCS codes G0425-G0427 If you provide services using CPT consultation codes, you should report the correct E/M visit code to bill for these services.

claims.text: D/C (discharge) — Discharge summary: outcome of the hospitalization, disposition of the case, and provisions for follow-up care; the final diagnosis is recorded and the record completed within 30 days after discharge.
claims.quote: (vii) Discharge summary with outcome of hospitalization, disposition of case, and provisions for follow-up care. (viii) Final diagnosis with completion of medical records within 30 days following discharge.

claims.text: D/C (discharge) — Hand-off at discharge: send the necessary medical information on the current course of illness and treatment, post-discharge goals of care and treatment preferences to the post-acute providers and practitioners responsible for follow-up care.
claims.quote: The hospital must discharge the patient, and also transfer or refer the patient where applicable, along with all necessary medical information pertaining to the patient's current course of illness and treatment, post-discharge goals of care, and treatment preferences, at the time of discharge, to the appropriate post-acute care service providers and suppliers, facilities, agencies, and other outpatient service providers and practitioners responsible for the patient's follow-up or ancillary care.
